items.title: IBM Has Raised Its Dividend for 31 Years. Inflation Is Still Winning
items.summary: IBM has raised its dividend for three decades straight, but the latest increase fits on a penny. Before counting on that income to keep pace with rising costs, retirees should understand what the streak actually delivers.

items.title: Did SMCI Stock Just Rise For The Wrong Reason?
items.summary: Super Micro Computer (SMCI) stock rose 9.5% on Thursday, September 17, closing just over $40. The move followed a bullish call on how big the market for AI servers gets. That call may well be right. But it answers a question Super Micro's own results never raised. That is why one big session tells you less than it looks like it does.

items.title: Cisco Drops 8% in 3 Months: Should You Buy the Stock on the Dip?
items.summary: CSCO's 8% three-month drop reflects margin and recurring-growth concerns, but surging AI demand and networking refresh opportunities support its outlook.

items.title: Can Hewlett Packard Enterprise Stock Keep Running On Orders It Cannot Ship?
items.summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) has returned 156% over the trailing twelve months, and the stock now sits right at the top of its 52-week range. The next leg is the hard one. What could power it is already on the company's books: orders it has taken and cannot yet ship.

items.title: The Options Market Says Dell Stock Can Halve Or Double
items.summary: Dell Technologies (DELL) stock trades at about $588, and the options market has already priced where it is most likely to sit twelve months from now: there is a two-in-three chance it lands between roughly $290 and roughly $1,180. That band is what a holder is carrying, in dollars. It prices the size of the move and says nothing about the direction. The size is the part worth your attention.

items.title: How Much Does Arista Networks Stock Move When The Market Moves?
items.summary: Arista Networks (ANET) has gained 5.6% over the last five trading days while the S&P 500 added 0.6%. A gap like that pulls buyers in. But the five-day move is not the question. The real one is what owning Arista does to your money every time the market moves, because it travels much further than the index in both directions.
